figures.title: The policy and effect-consumer boundary
figures.description: Grade settings are authoritative. The host supplies observations to a pure reducer, its effects authorize adapter operations, and operation receipts return as events.

figures.title: Latest-demand preparation scheduling
figures.description: The latest requested signature shares one physical preparation slot. Preview leaves the running job occupied; its final receipt starts the newest successor.

figures.title: The three-component preparation join
figures.description: The join tracks each pending child and retains the first error until all three preparations retire. Completed configurations are absorbing.

figures.title: Node output and installation policy
figures.description: Output is derived as current, preview, pending, or error. Only a full-quality installation for current demand can render; new demand can leave error.

figures.title: Helper process lifecycle
figures.description: All helper phases are explicit from startup through physical exit and cleanup. Failed can still close on shutdown; closed is absorbing. Receipts use generation and job identity.

figures.title: Production two-bank publication
figures.description: The inactive bank is staged before selector readback and delivery. Repair waits for output closure. Selection or delivery failure restores the old selector; confirmed closure and successful delivery share one terminal state.

figures.title: Immutable parameter-image publication
figures.description: This comparison strategy shows each stage, snapshot, binding, commit, activation, delivery, restoration, failure, and retirement phase. Failed transactions attempt each restoration component.

figures.title: Shared-image publication and restoration
figures.description: This comparison strategy shows snapshot, upload, packing, commit, delivery, and each restoration phase. A matching clean image skips upload and packing; failed restoration stops before metadata restoration.

figures.title: Compositor supersession protection
figures.description: The production PublicationGate sends completion and reset events to this policy. Its live admission and supersession path is used by the comparison example: supersession protects a scene and epoch until a later successful completion for that scene or a quiescent reset.

figures.title: Resource adoption and retirement
figures.description: Adoption is a predicate. Disposal fences and detaches subscriptions before observation; removal requires eviction and a fresh eligibility check. Terminal is shared by successful removal and ineligible outcomes.

figures.title: Observer handoff policy
figures.description: Observer installation promotes only a matching pending token. Separate states show pending installation with and without a current observer; reset preserves the monotonic serial.

figures.title: Gesture participation in the runtime coordinator
figures.description: The runtime tracks armed, active, finishing-armed, and finishing-active states. Scalar policy decisions release only the final active participant in a node.

figures.title: Render preflight authorization
figures.description: A waiting render ticket releases only after an exactly correlated published signature. Stale generations are ignored; current mismatches fail. Released and failed are absorbing states.

figures.title: Bake request and publication policy
figures.description: A correlated request progresses from queueing through native evaluation, admitted publication, and activation. Stale results are discarded; running cancellation retains ownership until a final receipt. Failed or stale publication and activation authorize rollback. Terminal is absorbing.

figures.title: Preparation and node output workflow
figures.description: A rapid settings edit retains the last installation as a preview while one worker prepares the latest demand. Existing publication effects append a native template, bind the current payload, validate and install it. A current preparation, template, binding, or installation failure selects visible error output.

figures.title: Preparation join workflow
figures.description: Linear, tone, and boundary workers run in parallel. The join accepts each distinct receipt, retains the first error, and emits completion only after all three retire.

figures.title: Helper process workflow
figures.description: The runtime launches and probes a helper, dispatches work, delivers preview and final receipts, handles optional cancellation, and escalates shutdown through termination, physical exit, and cleanup.

figures.title: Bank publication workflow
figures.description: A production bank is staged, selected with readback, delivered to Blender, or restored and failed closed. Staging appends and binds a bundled native template when the Grade graph needs replacement. Repair waits for confirmed output closure and closure retries are bounded.

figures.title: Immutable parameter publication workflow
figures.description: The comparison transaction stages, snapshots, binds, commits, activates, delivers, and retires an immutable image. Failure from binding through delivery attempts every binding, metadata, and resource restoration; earlier failure goes directly to failure output and retirement.

figures.title: Shared image publication workflow
figures.description: A matching clean snapshot skips upload and packing. Upload, packing, or commit failure attempts restoration; metadata is restored only if upload and packing restoration succeed. Other failure paths fail and retire directly.

figures.title: Compositor supersession workflow
figures.description: A compositor snapshot is admitted for one scene and epoch, superseded after binding, and protected from stale callbacks until a later successful evaluation or quiescent reset.

figures.title: Resource retirement workflow
figures.description: Disposal fences and detaches before observation. An eligible resource is evicted, rechecked, and removed; protected or in-use resources are retained.

figures.title: Observer and gesture workflow
figures.description: The coordinator installs and hands off an observer, tracks pointer movement, defers finish until native observation, and releases only the last active node participant.

figures.title: Render preflight workflow
figures.description: A render ticket waits for main-thread reconciliation and releases only for an exact published signature. Mismatches fail visibly; stale generations are ignored.

figures.title: Native bake and managed Image publication workflow
figures.description: The manager freezes current native trees and source pixels, serializes helper evaluation, and retains a ready artifact while publication is deferred. Publication, activation, and rollback share one admitted commit scope. Shared readers are synchronized after activation or restoration.
